model.name: Constraint / Requirement Rule
model.purpose: Represent one governed formal or formalizable rule that constrains, requires, permits or prohibits a subject under explicit applicability, authority and evaluation semantics.
model.scope_statement: Owns rule identity and immutable revision; source statement and normalized expression; rule kind, normative modality, severity, priority and criticality; issuer, owner, steward, subject, target, beneficiary and authority; rationale and evidence references; scope, jurisdiction, system boundary, applicability, trigger, preconditions and effective period; predicate, operands, variables, operators, datatypes, units, tolerance, cardinality, quantifiers and logical composition; dependencies and traceability; evaluation input, engine, profile, result and evidence; exceptions, waivers, conflicts and precedence; approval, effectivity, suspension, correction, retirement, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Requirement, policy, standard, control, system, object, actor, decision, test, observation, evidence, exception and enforcement masters remain external.
in_scope: Rule identity, source and normalized expression, kind, modality, revision and authority
Applicability, predicate, operands, datatypes, units, logic, dependency, traceability, evaluation and outcomes
Exceptions, conflicts, lifecycle, provenance, governance, access, retention and interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning stakeholder need, requirement record, policy, standard, control, system, object, actor, decision, test, observation, evidence, exception or enforcement lifecycles

Equating syntax validity with satisfaction, satisfaction with conformance, conformance with compliance, rule-engine output with accountable decision, or normative keyword with authority absent an adopting context
Executing approval, waiver, enforcement, protected disclosure, external system mutation, safety action or irreversible deletion

boundary_notes.distinction: Requirement owns the stakeholder need or governed requirement record. Constraint / Requirement Rule owns a separately reusable formal or formalizable normative expression; the candidate parent signal is held for review.
These authoritative packages may issue or group rules. Their identity, governance and lifecycle remain external while each rule preserves source and authority.
SHACL, JSON Schema and Schematron are executable projections. Schema syntax, engine conformance and validation reports do not replace rule identity or substantive intent.
A rule evaluation supplies a qualified result. Accountable decisions, remedies, sanctions and physical or digital enforcement remain external actions.
Tests and evidence support verification or assessment. A passed test or satisfied predicate does not by itself prove system validation, compliance, safety or legal effect.
The rule records bounded exception references and their effect on evaluation. The external authorization case and accountable approval remain independently mastered.
Engines evaluate pinned projections against input snapshots. Runtime, deployment, code, security and operational lifecycles remain external.

providerPolicy.scope: Canonical single-stream subject-model research after the six-workstream consolidation

waived_providers.reason: Claude produced no result on prior 1800-second and 900-second attempts and again timed out on bounded 600-second Sonnet and 300-second Haiku passes. The owner prioritized completion over provider availability.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.

providerPolicy.review_rule: Codex may complete source-grounded fallback research after bounded Claude and Grok attempts fail. It requires a separate no-tools adversarial audit and remains reviewable-draft with a visible absence-of-external-review hold.

supplemental_provider_attempts.admission_rule: Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.
Use only a locally schema-valid result whose sources and boundaries survive adjudication.

boundaryDecision.rationale: The root is a persistent versioned rule expression with its own identity, authority, applicability and evaluation contract. Evaluations, decisions and enforcement occur around it but do not turn the rule itself into an event.

decisions.rationale: The model owns one reusable rule and its immutable revisions rather than requirement-record authorship, validation execution or accountable enforcement.
A requirement may source or own the rule, but canonical inheritance requires joint boundary review because rules also originate in policies, standards and other authorities.
Requirement, constraint, invariant, business rule, validation shape, policy rule and legal norm use distinct modality and authority semantics.
Operands, operators, datatypes, units, logic, input snapshot, engine and profile must be source-qualified and versioned.
Syntax validity, satisfaction, verification, validation, conformance, compliance, safety, legal effect and accountable decision are separate claims.
Departures and precedence resolutions require explicit scope, authority, rationale, conditions, effective time and expiry while source rules remain visible.
OCL, DMN, SHACL, OWL, SPARQL, ODRL, LegalRuleML, XACML, JSON Schema, Schematron, OSCAL, OpenAPI and Rego views do not replace canonical rule identity.
Agents may append low-risk formalizations and evaluations but not approve, waive, enforce, disclose protected data or destroy records without authority.

decisions.concept: Provider waiver and local no-tools audit
decisions.rationale: One bounded Claude Sonnet attempt timed out and one bounded Grok attempt failed with stderr suppressed and hashed. Codex separately audits the frozen validated result and comparison without acquiring new facts, so assurance remains reviewable-draft.

publicationHolds: Absence-of-external-review hold: one Claude Sonnet attempt timed out and one Grok attempt failed before producing an admissible result; no external result was admitted.
Relation hold: WM-REC-006 remains a reference rather than an approved parent until joint boundary review.
Boundary hold: requirements, policies, standards, controls, systems, objects, tests, evidence, decisions, exceptions and enforcement actions remain external masters.
Profile hold: engineering, business, validation, legal, access-control, safety and compliance rules require domain-specific semantics.
Evaluation hold: syntax validity, rule satisfaction, verification, validation, conformance, compliance, safety and legal effect remain distinct.
Exception hold: waivers, deviations, conflicts and precedence require accountable authority, bounded scope, rationale and time.
Engine hold: executable evaluation requires pinned rule revision, input snapshot, engine, built-ins, profile, clock and outcome vocabulary.
Interoperability hold: every standards projection requires exact release pins, conformance tests and semantic-loss declarations.
Completeness hold: the 24-source draft is broad but does not claim universal domain, legal, logical, safety or operational coverage.
Independent external review was explicitly waived by the repository owner; this codex-only result remains a reviewable draft.

limits: WM-REC-006 is a reserved view-candidate with no current full specification; its boundary must be completed before publication.
WM-KNW-013 is a non-canonical reviewable draft with a single-provider waiver; registry relations and v1 fields remain non-normative.
